ideas.title: Fling me
ideas.critique: Pull-back-and-release is the most familiar toy gesture there is, and it is one more thing the player does with the mouse. What's strong is real soft-body deformation of Lumi's own mesh: stretch, splat, stick and peel off, with prints left on friends. The island has never had that, and people would fling it again and again. It only scores if the jelly reads as jelly in motion and the collisions are real, not keyframed.

ideas.title: Embers from the moon
ideas.critique: This is round 1's Hit the moon with the catapult taken out, so it loses the only part the player could play and becomes a night event to watch. Friends gathering round it like a campfire and one trying to eat it is a gag the island has run many times. Many small real lights that fall, smoulder and light faces from below are still a true path-tracer subject.

ideas.title: The sea is a mirror at noon
ideas.critique: Doubles of the friends walking around and replaying actions are Yesterday's ghosts, played in reverse this time. Nobody would need to watch the backwards gag twice. A sea that becomes a perfect mirror is a fair material showcase for the tracer, but the doubles are scripted copies, and noon is the flattest light the island has.

ideas.title: Snow globe on the table
ideas.critique: The player moves the whole island and the friends tumble. That is the seesaw and Keep the island level again, and a tiny live copy of the island was already done in My workshop, out at sea. Traced glass refraction is a real material step, and shaking it is a toy people would come back to. That only holds if friends and fruit truly fall under physics rather than wobbling on a script.
